text:
oliver: hey team, new hire question. rotated my hosted key and my local scripts started 401ing. Should I ever use hosted keys on my laptop or stick to sandbox keys?

tay: welcome! :wave: stick to sandbox for local dev. Hosted = production; keep it in secrets and staging/prod only.

oliver: how do I get a sandbox key? I only see Hosted in the UI.

devon: Console -> API keys -> Create sandbox key. If its not visible, SSO propagation might be delayed or your role may be restricted. Ping #devex if missing.

oliver: thanks found it. But sandbox rate limits are tiny

any tips to avoid 429s while iterating?

tay: a few quick ones: 1) local throttling (sleep 50-200ms), 2) exponential backoff honoring Retry-After, 3) mock or stub for unit tests, 4) request a short CI sandbox quota for integration tests via #devex template.

devex-bot: Template: "Quota request - repo:<repo>, purpose:<CI|staging|pairing>, expected RPS:<n>, duration:<24h|72h>, contact:@<handle>"

oliver: any sequence for rotating hosted keys used by services? I rotated in Console and forgot to update the secret store so services got 401s.

devon: recommended sequence: create new key in Console, update secret store (Vault/GH secrets), restart consumers so they pick up new value, then revoke old key. Confirm consumers are healthy before revoking.

infra-bot: :warning: Security policy: Do NOT commit hosted API keys. If exposed, rotate immediately and notify security@redwood.ai. Automated scanners will flag commits.

oliver: fixed my env, switched to sandbox for dev, and opened a devex ticket for a 48h CI sandbox key for integration tests. thanks! :thumbsup:
